entries.title: About the Course
entries.content:
Each year, students in Grades 3-6 read one of the gospels. For 2026-2027, they read John. Lesson plans include map work and assigned selections of The New Manners and Customs of Bible Times for teachers to read with their students before or after Bible reading to help give context and insight into the culture and geography of Israel during Jesus' life.

This topic is included in the following course(s): Bible: Grade 3, Bible: Grades 4-6

blocks.text:
• Connect to previous lessons by asking students to recall where they left off. 

• If students have difficulty recalling, teachers might try showing them a picture from the reading, sharing something the teacher remembers, or prompting them with the first sentence of the last reading. This will often refresh their memory enough to allow them to recall.

• If students still cannot recall anything from the last reading, teachers might consider continuing anyway (with a shorter reading this time) or repeating the previous lesson, depending on the reading and the nature of the book.

• Read the chapter or selection aloud. When reading to pre-readers, point to the words as you read, even if it seems they aren't paying attention.

• Move at the students' pace during the lesson, rather than feeling that a particular number of pages must be completed. It is vitally important that teachers not overload students with more material than they can absorb in one sitting.

• Students who have difficulty sitting still or listening may benefit from a fidget of their choice, such as a piece of putty or clay or an afghan; flexible positioning, such as a wobble seat or inverted sitting; or sensory modulation, such as a weighted vest or blanket or adjustment of light, temperature, or sound.

• Students with regular difficulty engaging often benefit from having a picture to associate with the story WHILE listening. Feel free to view the artwork during the reading rather than after the narration.

• Have students retell the passage orally.

• Alternatively, learners may use words, pictures, Legos, dolls, etc., to process and convey ideas in the manner most natural to them.  

• Teachers may take turns to model.

• Narration is a complex skill requiring the coordination of several parts of the brain. If a student struggles to narrate in general, with a specific subject or book, or on one day but not others, then this is an opportunity to learn. Observe when they struggle with this or any other activity today. Notice facial expressions and body language; listen to what they say about why it is hard or how they feel about it. Take note of these observations for later, tell them that you see how hard they are working, and then offer whatever support they need to end on a positive note. If necessary, take a break for the day.
• Optional: Share a piece of fine art that illustrates the story.
• Give students an opportunity to share their thoughts on the lesson and any connections made.

lessons.title: 20m New Testament: Grades 3-6 - Lesson 1
lessons.body:
Intro to the Gospel of John
⍞ Materials: ESV Large Print Bible, notebook

PREP:
Teachers may wish to view the Bible Project video covering the first half of the book of John in preparation for teaching. 
∞ Video Link: Bible Project: Book of John (First Half)

➜ INTRO
For our New Testament reading this year, we will be looking at the fourth Gospel in the New Testament, the book of John. The John who wrote the book is one of the twelve disciples who followed Jesus closely throughout his ministry on earth. He also wrote the books of First, Second, Third John, and the book of Revelation.
The book of John was written somewhere between 85-95 AD, which makes it the last of the four gospels written. In his gospel, John includes some details that the others left out and skips over some events that the other three gospel writers included. He writes to both Jews and Gentiles. (A Gentile is anyone who is not Jewish.) 

➜ READ & NARRATE
Today, we will look at a few verses to set a foundation for our reading this year and to find out a little bit about who John was. 
We do not have to guess why John wanted to write his gospel, because he states his purpose very clearly. 
Read John 20:30-31.

• Why does John say he wrote his gospel? 

Read John 13:23; 20:2; 21:7, 20.

• How does John speak about himself in relation to Jesus? 

Read Matthew 4:18-22; Mark 3:13-21.

• How do the gospel authors Matthew and Mark refer to John? 

➜ NOTEBOOK 
As you read through the book of John, you will keep a notebook. Today, you will begin this notebook by making a title page. 
On your title page, write the name of the book, the author, and the approximate date the book was written, 85-95 AD. On your title page, copy down John 20:30-31, the verses stating the purpose of the book. (Students may write as little or as much as time and ability allow. You could also take time to complete this task in lesson 2, if needed.)

links.text: Bible Project: Book of John (First Half)

lessons.title: 20m New Testament: Grades 3-6 - Lesson 2
lessons.body:
The Word Was God
⍞ Materials: ESV Large Print Bible, notebook (optional)

NOTE: Today's lesson has a video that is a helpful explanation of the opening of John's gospel. Although some of the concepts may be a bit intricate for younger students, the overall look at this passage gives helpful context to John's opening words. 

➜ RECAP
What do you recall about what we read about last time about the introduction to the book of John? 

➜INTRO
Instead of starting with the birth of Jesus or with the story of John the Baptist, as the other three gospels do, John begins his gospel by showing that Jesus is the Son of God and is 100% God and 100% human. 
The book of John starts with "In the beginning." This reminds us of Genesis 1:1, the very first verse of the Bible, which begins with the exact same phrase: In the beginning.  
Also, in today's reading, another man named John the Baptist is mentioned. These are two separate individuals with the same name. John, the author, tells us what the role of John the Baptist was. 

➜ READ & NARRATE
John 1:1-13

➜ VIEW & NARRATE
Watch the video for an overview and explanation of John 1. 
∞ Video Link: John 1

➜ NOTEBOOK (Optional)
If additional time was needed to copy down verse 20:30-31, you may complete that today.

lessons.title: 20m New Testament: Grades 3-6 - Lesson 3
lessons.body:
The Word Dwelt Among Us
⍞ Materials: ESV Large Print Bible, notebook 

➜ RECAP
What do you recall about our reading last time in the book of John? 

➜ READ & NARRATE
John 1:14-27

➜ READ & NARRATE
∞ Article Link: What does it mean that the Word dwelt among us?
For younger students: Begin with the fourth paragraph "Not only did the Word" - end.
Older students: Read the entire answer starting with "In John 1:14."

➜ NOTEBOOK 
Younger students may draw a picture of what we have read so far in John or write a short summary. Older students may write a longer summary or write down what they have learned about Jesus dwelling, or being "tabernacled," among us.

links.text: What does it mean that the Word dwelt among us?

lessons.title: 20m New Testament: Grades 3-6 - Lesson 4
lessons.body:
Behold! 
⍞ Materials: ESV Large Print Bible, notebook 

➜ RECAP
What do you recall about our reading last time in the book of John? 

➜ INTRO
The next verses continue speaking about John the Baptist and his testimony regarding his baptizing of Jesus. He testifies to Jesus, and the people who hear him begin following Jesus. As the Bible Project states, "One by one as people encounter Jesus, they say out loud who they think he is. In this one chapter, Jesus is given seven titles: the Lamb of God, Son of God, Rabbi, Messiah, King of Israel, Jesus of Nazareth, and the Son of Man."

Today, we will begin a list of the titles people give when they see Jesus, and in our next reading, we will read the rest of these titles. These seven titles claim Jesus as the Messiah and Savior of the world. 

In the passage, we also see Jesus call his first two disciples. In New Testament times, it was not unusual for Rabbis—or Teachers—to have disciples who would follow and learn from these teachers. 

➜ READ & NARRATE
John 1:28-39
• As Simon Peter and Andrew did, what would it be like to drop everything and begin following Jesus as his disciple? 

➜ NOTEBOOK 
Younger students, draw a picture either of John the Baptist speaking about Jesus OR of Simon Peter and Andrew following after Jesus. Older students may write a summary or begin a list of the seven names given to Jesus in this chapter. (The three from today's reading would be: Lamb of God, Rabbi (Teacher), and Messiah (Christ).) Write the name and the verse reference where the title is found.

lessons.title: 20m New Testament: Grades 3-6 - Lesson 6
lessons.body:
Wedding at Cana
⍞ Materials: ESV Large Print Bible, notebook

➜ RECAP
What do you recall about our reading last time in the book of John? 

➜ INTRO
John's gospel includes signs to point to Jesus as Messiah. These miracles (signs) are contained in the first few chapters of the book, and some refer to chapters 1-12 as "The Book of Signs." In John's purpose statement for his gospel, he stated that Jesus did many signs during his ministry on earth, and these miracles or signs are included so that people would believe Jesus was the Messiah (John 20:30-31). In other words, these signs were pointing to who Jesus is. Today's reading will include the first of these signs. 

➜ READ & NARRATE
John 2:1-12
Weddings often went on for seven days, and frequently the best wine would be served at the beginning, with the less expensive (not as good) wine being held to the last. However, when they taste the wine Jesus has provided, it is much better than even the expensive wine! Jesus as the Creator is shown through this miracle. And, even today, we see that God uses rain to water the vineyards to grow the grapes to turn into wine in the "agricultural and fermentation processes. Here He simply did the process immediately." (The Bible Knowledge Commentary)

➜ VIEW & DISCUSS
∞ Image Link: The Marriage at Cana by Paolo Veronese

• What do you notice about this painting of how the artist depicted the wedding at Cana? 

➜ NOTEBOOK 
Turn in your notebook to a blank page (you may want to leave space for 2 pages if writing or 3-4 pages if the student will be drawing), where we will begin to create a list of the signs John includes in his gospel. Younger students: Begin your list with the number 1. Either write down a summary phrase (i.e., Jesus turns water into wine at the wedding) or draw a picture to show what the first sign is. Older students may title their list, and under 1., write down a summary phrase, verse reference, and description of what Jesus' first miracle was.

lessons.title: 20m New Testament: Grades 3-6 - Lesson 8
lessons.body:
Nicodemus
⍞ Materials: ESV Large Print Bible, notebook

➜ RECAP
What do you recall about our reading last time in the book of John? 

➜ INTRO
Nicodemus, a leader of the Jews, came to meet with Jesus to ask questions. "Jesus told Nicodemus how he could see the kingdom of God and how to be born again - by believing in Jesus, God's Son. Jesus came to give eternal life to those who believe." (Bible Story Handbook) 

➜ READ & NARRATE
John 3:1-21
• Do you think this is the answer Nicodemus was expecting when he came to visit Jesus? Why or why not? 

➜NOTEBOOK 
Younger students may draw a picture of Nicodemus asking his question or write a short summary. Older students may write a longer summary of Nicodemus talking to Jesus and Jesus' response.

lessons.title: 20m New Testament: Grades 3-6 - Lesson 9
lessons.body:
John the Baptist is Pointing at Jesus
⍞ Materials: ESV Large Print Bible; Student Bible Atlas

➜ RECAP
What do you recall about our reading last time in the book of John? 

➜ INTRO
John, the disciple writing the account, shifts his focus to a response John the Baptist gave to those who questioned him. 

➜ READ & NARRATE
John 3:22-36
"For a short time the ministry of John the Baptist overlapped Jesus' ministry." John the Baptist had always known he was pointing to the coming Messiah, and now that Jesus was here, "Jesus must become greater and John must become less....John willingly and with joy accepted Jesus' growing popularity as God's plan." (Bible Knowledge Commentary)

➜ MAP WORK
Let's look at the map of the area Jesus is ministering in. Find the locations marked below where events have taken place in the first three chapters of John.
⍞ Map Resource: Student Bible Atlas Maps 19-20 p.22-23 (Either map can be used for all but Jerusalem and Judea, which are only shown on Map 19.)
Read the text box p.23 "Jesus in Galilee." 
1\. Locate Nazareth - the town where Jesus is from. 
2\. Locate Cana - where Jesus performed his first miracle.
3\. Locate Capernaum on the shore of the Sea of Galilee.
4\. Locate Jerusalem (Map 19 p.22).
5\. Locate Judea  - referred to as Judean countryside (3:22). (This is the pink shaded area on Map 19.)

lessons.title: 20m New Testament: Grades 3-6 - Lesson 10
lessons.body:
Woman at the Well 
⍞ Materials: ESV Large Print Bible, notebook

➜ RECAP
What do you recall about our reading last time in the book of John? 

➜ INTRO
John's gospel moves from Jesus meeting with Nicodemus, a high-ranking Jewish leader, to telling of Jesus meeting a Samaritan woman, who would have been seen as a person of low rank. The Jewish people hated the people group known as the Samaritans, and as they traveled, they would go out of their way to avoid walking through Samaria. However, today we will see that Jesus chose to walk through Samaria, where he met this Samaritan woman at a well. Imagine the long walk: "This three-day journey encompasses over seventy miles of rugged rock roads in a hot, dry climate. Your face is beet red from the heat, your body is sweating, and your mouth is parched dry - my, what you wouldn't give for a drink of water! Are you there yet? You're relieved when the tired and sore feet of Jesus take refuge during the heat of the noonday sun at Jacob's well. Finally, a water break!" (The Gospel of John, Armijo, Mitchell and Krause)

➜ READ & NARRATE
John 4:1-15
After the long, hot walk, the water from the well would definitely satisfy the traveler's thirst, but Jesus speaks to the woman about a living water that will satisfy her thirst forever. "...The water Jesus gives provides continual satisfaction of needs and desires. In addition one who drinks His living water will have within him a spring of life-giving water... Jesus was speaking of the Holy Spirit who brings salvation to a person who believes and through Him offers salvation to others." (Bible Knowledge Commentary) John includes these stories to show that Jesus' message of salvation was available to all—whether you were a Jewish leader or a Samaritan woman at a well. 

➜ NOTEBOOK 
Younger students: Draw a picture of the woman at the well meeting Jesus or write a short summary. Older students may write a longer summary or copy down one or more verses from today's passage.

➜ NOTEBOOK (Optional)

lessons.title: 20m New Testament: Grades 3-6 - Lesson 13
lessons.body:
Jesus Heals an Official's Son
⍞ Materials: ESV Large Print Bible, notebook

➜ RECAP
What do you recall about our reading last time in the book of John? 

➜ READ & NARRATE
John 4:43-5:1
The official comes from Capernaum to Cana, which is approximately 20 to 25 miles, desiring that Jesus heal his son. When Jesus replies that his son is healed, the official had to believe in Cana that Jesus had healed his son back in Capernaum. The official asked his servants when his son had been healed, and it was at the exact time Jesus had "made his promise to him...Jesus' power is able to save from death even at a great distance. His word has power to work." (Bible Knowledge Commentary) John points out in 4:54 that this was the second sign.

➜ NOTEBOOK 
Turn in your notebook to your list of signs to add the miracle of Jesus healing the official's son. Younger students: Next to 2., either write down a summary phrase or draw a picture to depict this second sign. Older students may add to your list by writing down a summary phrase, verse reference, and description of what Jesus' second sign was.

⍞ Materials: ESV Large Print Bible, Student Bible Atlas, notebook

➜ RECAP
What do you recall about our reading last time in the book of John? 

➜ READ & NARRATE
John 5:2-17
This healing of the man at the pool of Bethesda is the third sign Jesus performed to show that he not only had power from God but also the right to claim to be the Son of God and equal with God.

➜ MAP WORK
⍞ Map Resource: Jerusalem at the Time of Christ Map 21 p.24
Locate the Pool of Bethesda. How close is it to the temple? 

➜ NOTEBOOK 
Turn in your notebook to your list of signs to add the miracle of healing at the Pool of Bethesda. Younger students: Next to 3., either write down a summary phrase or draw a picture to show what the third sign is. Older students may add to your list by writing down a summary phrase, verse reference, and description of what Jesus' third miracle was.

lessons.title: 20m New Testament: Grades 3-6 - Lesson 16
lessons.body:
A Witness 
⍞ Materials: ESV Large Print Bible

➜ RECAP
What do you recall about our reading last time in the book of John? 

In today's reading, the word "witness" is used. What is a witness? In John's gospel, this idea of a witness or testimony is important. At the start of his gospel, he tells about John the Baptist, a man whose "function was that of a witness. A good witness tells the truth as he knows it...Jesus did not need human testimony, but John's work helped people because in their darkness he pointed them to the light." John the Baptist did not perform any miracles, however. "The 'signs' were specific works which God assigned for the Son to do." This showed that God affirmed who Jesus was and witnessed to who Jesus was. (Bible Knowledge Commentary)

➜ READ & NARRATE
John 5:30-47

lessons.title: 20m New Testament: Grades 3-6 - Lesson 17
lessons.body:
Feeding of the 5,000
⍞ Materials: ESV Large Print Bible; Manners & Customs; notebook

➜ RECAP
What do you recall about our reading last time in the book of John? 

➜ READ & NARRATE
John 6:1-15
• The feeding of the 5,000 is the only miracle that is included in all four gospels, other than the resurrection of Jesus. Why do you think it is an important miracle to the writers of the gospels? 
 
➜ READ & NARRATE
Manners & Customs "Baking Bread" p.43-44
• Does knowing more about the process of baking bread in New Testament times make the story of Jesus miraculously multiplying loaves of bread even more amazing? Why or why not? 

➜ NOTEBOOK 
Turn in your notebook to your list of signs to add the feeding of the 5,000. Younger students: Next to 4., either write down a summary phrase or draw a picture to show what the fourth sign is. Older students may add to your list by writing down a summary phrase, verse reference, and description of what Jesus' fourth miracle was.

lessons.title: 20m New Testament: Grades 3-6 - Lesson 18
lessons.body:
Jesus Walks on Water
⍞ Materials: ESV Large Print Bible, notebook

➜ RECAP
What do you recall about our reading last time in the book of John? 

➜ READ & NARRATE
John 6:16-34
While we do not know exactly what this boat looked like, a boat was found from the Sea of Galilee, and it was about "twenty-five feet long and nearly eight feet wide. It could carry about a dozen men, perhaps as many as sixteen. Such boats were equipped with oars; some had simple masts as well, though a sail was not used in a storm. Because of the atmospheric conditions that result from the Sea of Galilee being nestled between mountains, wind storms are frequent, come on rapidly, and can be severe." (Bible Story Handbook)
• What would it have been like to be a disciple in a storm on a boat and then look out to see Jesus miraculously walking on water toward you? 

➜ NOTEBOOK 
Younger students may draw a picture or write a short summary of today's passage, while older students may write a longer summary or copy down a verse or more from the passage.

➜ READ & NARRATE

➜ NOTEBOOK 
While we continue our list of signs, we are also going to start a new list of Jesus' "I Am" statements found in the book of John. Turn in your notebook to a two-page spread, or (if drawing), turn to where you have 3 or 4 blank pages. Begin by writing the title (use your own words if you would like!): "I AM Statements by Jesus"
Younger students: Write the number 1., then draw a symbol or picture of the first "I Am" statement of Jesus. (i.e., Draw a loaf of bread.)
Older students: Number your list and write a short statement or summary of Jesus' first "I Am" statement. Include the verse reference.

lessons.title: 20m New Testament: Grades 3-6 - Lesson 30
lessons.body:
The Truth Will Set You Free
⍞ Materials: ESV Large Print Bible

➜ RECAP
What do you recall about what we read last time? 

➜ INTRO
As mentioned previously, John focuses on truth throughout his gospel and does so again in today's reading. Why do you think truth was an important point in John's message? 

➜ READ & NARRATE
John 8:31-47

• As Jesus answers the people, he states that there is no truth in the devil and his message. How does this contrast with the message and person of Jesus? (v.31)
• Do you recall John's purpose statement about why he is writing the book of John? (See 20:30-31 if needed.) How does knowing this help answer the question of why truth was important to John?

➜ RECAP

➜ INTRO
Over the next couple of New Testament lessons, the reading will tell us of Jesus healing a blind man. "This extensive healing account is the climactic sign of the first section of the Gospel as it details a particularly extraordinary healing and includes lengthy discussion of the healed man with the religious leaders over the nature of Jesus, particularly the unlearned man's rebuke of the leaders." (Bible Story Handbook)

➜ READ & NARRATE
John 8:48-9:7

➜ READ & NARRATE
Manners & Customs "Medicine in Jesus' time" p.156-157

➜NOTEBOOK 
The next sign is Jesus healing the blind man. Add this to your list in your notebook. Younger students could do this by drawing a picture or writing a short summary of the miracle. Older students can add the miracle to their list, the reference where it is found, and a summary of what happened.

lessons.title: 20m New Testament: Grades 3-6 - Lesson 36
lessons.body:
Lazarus
⍞ Materials: ESV Large Print Bible

➜ RECAP
What do you recall about what we read last time? 

➜ INTRO
As we have seen, the first part of John's gospel contains specific signs Jesus performed during his ministry on earth for the purpose of pointing to who he is. He shows power over nature, over creation, and now, in the next sign, he shows power over death. 

➜ READ & NARRATE
John 11:1-16
"Lazarus died soon after the messengers went to find Jesus. Jesus delayed his arrival so as to leave no doubt that Lazarus was dead. By the time of arrival, the body had been buried and had begun to decay. All this was essential for Jesus to display his power." (Bible Story Handbook) Our passage will continue next time with what happens next with the story of Lazarus.

lessons.title: 20m New Testament: Grades 3-6 - Lesson 37
lessons.body:
I Am the Resurrection and the Life
⍞ Materials: ESV Large Print Bible, notebook

➜ RECAP
What do you recall about what we read last time? 

➜ INTRO
"Determining physical death was more difficult in those days, so three days were allotted before doing so. By then, lack of water and nourishment would have ensured death. Burial usually took place the same day as the death, and the bodies were interred in a cave, not buried under the earth." (Bible Story Handbook)

➜ READ & NARRATE
John 11:17-37
In today's reading, Jesus states another I Am statement, saying that he is the Resurrection and the Life. For the believer who trusts in Jesus, they will have eternal life (3:16; 11:25-27). In verse 27, Martha responds to Jesus with her own confession of belief, stating three things about Jesus: He is the Christ, the Son of God, and the one who was to come into the world. While she had yet to see the miracle that was about to occur, she believed in who Jesus said he was. 

➜ NOTEBOOK 
In your notebook, open to your list of "I Am" statements Jesus has made and add: "I Am the Resurrection and the Life." Younger students may do this with a drawing of a symbol or a short statement. Older students may write a summary and include verse references, as well.

lessons.title: 20m New Testament: Grades 3-6 - Lesson 38

Lazarus Rises from the Dead
⍞ Materials: ESV Large Print Bible, notebook

➜ RECAP
What do you recall about what we read last time? 

➜ READ & NARRATE
John 11:38-54
Raising Lazarus from the dead is the final sign included in John's gospel. John included these signs to point to Jesus and who he is. "The reason he has power over death is that he is the source of life." 

• In verse 47, the Pharisees are quoted as saying, "What are we to do? For this man performs many signs." They are also seeing the signs pointing to Jesus, but what is their response to him after he raises Lazarus from the dead? 

➜NOTEBOOK 
In your notebook, add the raising of Lazarus from the dead to your list of signs John includes. Younger students may draw a picture of Lazarus, Mary, and Martha or write a short summary of the miracle. Older students may write a longer summary or copy down key verses from the passage.

⍞ Materials: ESV Large Print Bible

Although these signs were to point people to Jesus and who he is, many did not believe. In today's reading, Jesus will speak about this and affirm his message that he came to save the world. Although he would soon be crucified on the cross, those who were listening did not fully understand this was to happen. 

➜ READ & NARRATE
John 12:27-38

➜ VIEW & DISCUSS
⍞ Image Resource: The Entry of Christ into Jerusalem 
All of this was happening right after the resurrection of Lazarus and the triumphal entry of Jesus into Jerusalem. While some were celebrating and shouting "Hosanna!," some were angry and upset with Jesus. Let's take some time to view an image of how an artist envisioned Jesus entering Jerusalem. What do you notice about the painting?

• In the area where the gospel of John took place, it was dry and dusty, so foot washing was a regular part of being hospitable. Typically, this task was done by a servant who would pour water over the guest's feet into a bowl and then dry the feet off. What is Jesus showing his disciples by being the one who washed their feet?

The same combination of human obedience to the divine command (Acts 1:8) coupled with the witness of the Spirit is needed in every generation." (Bible Knowledge Commentary)

• When Nicodemus had come to talk to Jesus in the night (John 3), John did not include what Nicodemus' response was. However, here we see Nicodemus help Joseph with the body of Jesus. Nicodemus had seen the "Son of Man be lifted up" (3:14) on the cross, in other words, what Jesus had told him had now come to pass. Based on this, how do you think Jesus' talk with him had impacted Nicodemus?
